edits.value_json: 月 is a pictograph of a half moon. Shang inscriptions attest it both for the moon and for a calendar month; the latter use is associated with the moon’s waxing and waning, though the order of these uses is unresolved.

The whole graph depicts a half moon; the evidence identifies no smaller semantic or phonetic components. Early forms are described as moon pictures. Bronze forms continue that graphic line, while the small-seal form is reported to have changed; the precise change is not established here.

The selected oracle-script image is a modern rendering linked to a specific Sinica record; the selected seal-script image is a modern reconstruction of the Shuowen tradition. They compare graphic forms but do not establish a precise sequence or first attestation.

月 is used for the moon in current Chinese, and Shang oracle-bone examples attest the same use, including in an eclipse context. These are early examples, but the precise first dated occurrence is not established here.
